exposure: Hospitalization for hyperemesis gravidarum during the first and second trimester of pregnancy
outcome: Intrapartum complications attributed to placental dysfunction disorders
cohort: The study recruited 250 women with singleton pregnancies who experienced at least one hospitalization for hyperemesis gravidarum, followed from gestational age >10 to >21 completed weeks until delivery.
finding: Hospitalization for hyperemesis gravidarum in the first and second trimesters was significantly associated with a higher incidence of intrapartum complications attributed to placental dysfunction disorders.
gest_age: Participants were singleton pregnancies with gestational age >10 to >21 completed weeks at recruitment, with admission for hyperemesis gravidarum occurring at <10 weeks or >12 to 21 completed weeks.
